body.stem: You created a subscription for a customer whose Microsoft Entra directory differs from your own. Subscriptions > View requests now shows the entry below. Which statement best describes the current state of the request and what you should do?

options.text: It expired, so create a new request and send the customer the accept ownership link
It's still active, so resend the same accept ownership link for the request to the customer
The subscription already exists in the target directory and the request only needs an owner assigned
It expired, and the request was auto-approved so the subscription was created in the source directory

explanation.correct: When someone creates a subscription for a customer in another directory, the request must be accepted by the subscription owner in the target directory within seven days; otherwise the request expires and nothing is created. The exhibit shows the request was created on 2 October and checked on 21 October, so the seven-day window has passed and the request is no longer usable. The requester has to create a fresh subscription creation request and can copy the accept ownership URL from the request details and send it manually to the customer.

perChoice.b: A request like this stays usable for only seven days; it doesn't remain active indefinitely, and an old acceptance link can't revive it.
perChoice.c: No subscription exists in the customer's directory until the owner accepts the request, and owners are selected as part of creating the request rather than added afterward.
perChoice.d: Requests aren't auto-approved after the window closes, and even a valid request never puts the subscription in the source directory, because it belongs to the customer's directory once it is accepted.

body.stem: Your team is closing subscription sub-0199, and only the assignments listed below apply to it. Which user can run the cancellation in the Azure portal?

options.text: The user whose Owner assignment on the subscription has no condition applied
The user whose Owner assignment on the subscription has a condition applied
The user who holds only the Account Administrator role on the billing account
The user who holds only the Contributor role on the subscription

explanation.correct: For every subscription type covered by the documentation — pay-as-you-go, Visual Studio, Microsoft Enterprise Agreement and Azure plan subscriptions — the person who can cancel is the subscription owner whose Owner role assignment carries no condition. Dana's Owner assignment on /subscriptions/sub-0199 has no conditions, so Dana meets the requirement.

perChoice.b: Erin's Owner assignment is conditional (it requires multi-factor authentication), and the cancellation permission requires an Owner role assignment without a condition, so a Cancel option isn't available to Erin.
perChoice.c: An account administrator who doesn't also hold an unconditional subscription Owner role assignment can't cancel the subscription, which is why Femi can't.
perChoice.d: Contributor grants resource permissions but not subscription cancellation, so Gil can't cancel even though the role is scoped to the subscription.

body.stem: Two days ago you canceled subscription sub-0442. Today you select Delete on the subscription page in the Azure portal and the page shows the checklist below. Which action lets you complete the deletion?

options.text: Delete the 2 remaining resources, then wait until the manual deletion date has passed
Delete the 2 remaining resources and select Delete again right away, before the manual deletion date arrives
Have an account administrator delete the 2 resources, which waives the manual deletion date requirement
Wait 90 days and let Azure delete the 2 resources and the subscription automatically

explanation.correct: Both conditions on the page must be satisfied before the subscription can be deleted. Because the Delete resources check shows a red X, the remaining resources must be deleted first — including hidden types, which you reveal with Show hidden types on the subscription's Resources page — and resource deletion status can take up to 10 minutes to update. Because the manual deletion date check is also failing, you must wait until that period has elapsed: the Delete option isn't available until 3 days after cancellation for customer-led subscriptions, or 7 days for field and partner channel subscriptions.

perChoice.b: Deleting the resources is only half of it: the Delete option stays unavailable until the waiting period after cancellation has elapsed, so selecting it immediately fails.
perChoice.c: No role can shorten or waive the period after cancellation. An account administrator's help doesn't remove the manual deletion date requirement, and the resources still have to be deleted by someone.
perChoice.d: Azure's automatic deletion of a canceled subscription after 90 days doesn't remove the resources inside it; resources — and any hidden resources — have to be deleted manually, and waiting 90 days isn't a way to satisfy the checklist now.

body.stem: You are transferring billing ownership of subscription sub-2288 to an administrator in a different Microsoft Entra directory. The Transfer billing ownership page shows the values below. Your operations team must keep managing the subscription's resources after the transfer completes. Which change should you make before sending the request?

options.text: Clear Move subscription tenant so the subscription stays in the current directory
Select Move subscription tenant so the subscription moves to the receiving account's directory
Clear Move subscription tenant, then have each operations team member accept a separate request in the current directory
Select Move subscription tenant so the subscription moves to the receiving account's directory, and re-add each operations team member afterwards

explanation.correct: Clearing Move subscription tenant transfers billing ownership without moving the subscription to the new account's directory, and existing Azure role assignments to the subscription and its resources are maintained. That is what keeps the operations team able to manage the resources after the transfer. With the option selected, all role assignments are permanently removed instead.

perChoice.b: Selecting the option permanently removes all Azure role assignments that give access to the subscription and its resources; only the user in the new account who accepts the request keeps access, which is exactly the outcome the team wants to avoid.
perChoice.c: Clearing the option is the right control, but no per-user acceptance step follows it: role assignments already in place remain valid, so there's nothing for each team member to accept.
perChoice.d: Moving the subscription is what strips the existing assignments, and sending the request doesn't re-create them. If the subscription is moved, the new owner would have to add each user again after the transfer.

body.stem: You select Transfer billing ownership for subscription sub-3310 and the portal returns an Access denied error. The subscription was purchased under an Azure plan. Which permission do you need before you can send the transfer request?

options.text: Owner or contributor role on the invoice section for the subscription
Owner or contributor role on the management group the subscription is associated with
Owner or contributor role on the resource group that holds the subscription's resources
Owner or contributor role on the billing account

explanation.correct: An Access denied error when transferring billing ownership of a Microsoft Azure Plan subscription means you lack the required permission: you must be an owner or a contributor on the invoice section to which the subscription is billed. The assignments in the exhibit are scoped to a management group and a resource group, so neither of them satisfies that requirement.

perChoice.b: Holding Owner on the management group lets you administer what the management group contains, but it isn't the permission that authorizes transferring billing ownership of an Azure plan subscription.
perChoice.c: A Contributor assignment scoped to a resource group governs managing resources in that group; it doesn't grant any transfer permission on the subscription itself.
perChoice.d: For an Azure plan subscription the documented requirement is owner or contributor on the invoice section, not on the billing account, so this assignment still leaves you with the Access denied error.

body.stem: You have canceled the final subscription in a billing account this morning. Finance needs to know when the estimated charges shown at cancellation will be billed. Which statement should you give them?

rows: Subscriptions remaining in the billing account

options.text: Charging stops on 21 October, and the estimated charges are invoiced on 31 October, the current billing cycle end date, with no further delay.
Charging stops on 21 October, and the estimated charges are invoiced after the current billing cycle ends, up to three days later.
The estimated charges are invoiced on 21 October, and charging continues until the current billing cycle ends on 31 October.
Charging continues until the current billing cycle ends on 31 October, and the estimated charges are invoiced up to three days after that date.

explanation.correct: After you cancel, billing is stopped immediately, so nothing accrues after the cancellation timestamp. The estimated charges that aren't invoiced yet are carried over and appear on the final invoice, which is sent on the usual invoice date after the current billing period ends. Because the cycle can take up to 72 hours (three calendar days) to close and have the estimated charges updated, the bill can reach finance as late as roughly 3 November for a cycle that ends on 31 October.

perChoice.a: This assumes the invoice lands exactly on the cycle end date. The billing cycle can take up to 72 hours (three calendar days) after it ends to close and update estimated charges, so the final bill may arrive later than 31 October.
perChoice.c: This has the timing backwards on both points. Billing stops immediately at cancellation, and the estimated charges are not invoiced on the cancellation date — they appear on the invoice that follows the end of the billing period.
perChoice.d: The first half is wrong: charging does not continue after you cancel, it stops immediately. Only the invoicing of the estimated charges is deferred until the billing cycle ends.

body.stem: You have the role assignments listed below in a tenant whose Azure spend is administered through a Microsoft Customer Agreement billing account. You need to create a new subscription for yourself from the Azure portal. Which role assignment do you need to add?

options.text: Azure subscription creator on the invoice section
Azure subscription creator on the billing account
Azure subscription reader on the invoice section
Contributor on the management group MG-West

explanation.correct: To create a subscription for a Microsoft Customer Agreement you need owner or contributor on the invoice section, billing profile, or billing account, or the Azure subscription creator role on the invoice section. None of the assignments in the exhibit meets that bar: a billing account reader only reads billing data, a Reader on a resource group and a Contributor on a management group are resource-management permissions inside existing scopes. Adding the Azure subscription creator role on the invoice section is what enables the portal to create the subscription.

perChoice.b: The creator role is only sufficient at the invoice section scope. Granted at the billing account scope it doesn't satisfy the requirement; at that level it would be owner or contributor on the billing account that qualifies.
perChoice.c: A reader role lets you view the invoice section but not create subscriptions. Creation requires owner or contributor on the invoice section, billing profile, or billing account, or the Azure subscription creator role on the invoice section.
perChoice.d: Contributor on a management group lets you manage resources of the subscriptions in that group, but it doesn't grant permission to create new billing objects such as subscriptions.

body.stem: You have sent a billing ownership request for a Visual Studio Enterprise subscription to another account, and it has been completed today. Your finance team needs to know how the monthly credit behaves from now on. Which statement should you give them?

options.text: The subscription keeps drawing credit from the account it was transferred from until the end of the calendar month.
The subscription draws credit from the account it was transferred to, and that credit resets every ninth day of the month.
The subscription keeps the credit it carried over with the transfer, and that credit resets on the same day every month.

The credit in the account it was transferred to is not available to the subscription, but the subscription keeps drawing credit from the account it was transferred from, and that credit resets every ninth day of the month.

explanation.correct: Visual Studio and Microsoft Cloud Partner Program subscriptions carry monthly recurring credit. That credit isn't available in the receiving billing account as a carried-over balance: once the transfer completes, the subscription starts using the credit of the account that took it over, and that credit resets every ninth day of the month.

perChoice.a: The source account's credit doesn't remain attached to the subscription. As soon as the transfer completes, the subscription starts using the credit of the account that accepted it, so the switch happens right away rather than at the end of the calendar month.
perChoice.c: Nothing is carried across with the subscription — the credit held by the old billing account isn't available in the new one. The subscription simply uses the credit belonging to the account that took it over.
perChoice.d: The reset pattern is right but the account is wrong. The credit of the account that received the subscription is the one the subscription uses; the credit sitting in the old account is no longer available to it.

body.stem: You are standardizing how new Azure subscriptions get created across your organization. Match each rule below to the requirement that it enforces.

items.text: Development and testing workloads use Microsoft Azure Plan for DevTest; every other workload uses Microsoft Azure Plan
Owners can only be users or service principals from the subscription directory, and guest directory users are excluded
The subscription is linked to a management group that belongs to the directory you are signed in to
The subscription is created in a Microsoft Entra tenant, because B2B and B2C directories can't hold Azure resources
Management groups from any directory can be linked, so subscriptions can sit under a hierarchy that lives in another tenant
Guest directory users can be listed as owners once they have accepted an invitation

slots.label: Separate environments by purpose
Grant a non-human identity administrative access
Keep the governance hierarchy inside the current tenant
Make sure anything you want to deploy afterwards will work

explanation.correct: Each rule enforces one requirement: the DevTest plan is used for development and testing workloads while the standard plan is used otherwise, which keeps the two kinds of environment separate; subscription owners are limited to users and service principals from the selected subscription directory, so a non-human identity such as a service principal can be granted access; management groups can only be selected from the directory you are signed in to, which keeps the hierarchy inside the current tenant; and Azure resources such as subscriptions can only be provisioned in a Microsoft Entra tenant, not in a B2B or B2C tenant.

perChoice.i1: Fits the first requirement: Microsoft Azure Plan for DevTest is selected when the subscription is used for development or testing workloads, and Microsoft Azure Plan otherwise, which separates the environments by purpose.
perChoice.i2: Fits the second requirement: owners can be selected only among users and service principals in the chosen subscription directory, so an app registration can get administrative access, while guest directory users are excluded.
perChoice.i3: Fits the third requirement: management groups can be selected only from the directory you are signed in to, which keeps the hierarchy inside the current tenant.
perChoice.i4: Fits the fourth requirement: subscriptions and other Azure resources must be provisioned in a Microsoft Entra tenant, because a B2B or B2C tenant can't hold them.
perChoice.i5: Incorrect: only management groups in the current directory can be selected, so a subscription can't be linked to a hierarchy that lives in another tenant.
perChoice.i6: Incorrect: guest directory users can't be chosen in the owners picker, whether or not they accepted an invitation.

body.stem: You canceled your last Azure subscription this morning, and your finance lead wants a timeline of what happens next. Match each event below to the point on that timeline where it happens.

items.text: Charging for usage stops
The invoice covering the usage just consumed is issued, up to three calendar days later
The Delete option becomes available to you
Anything kept afterwards is destroyed somewhere between 30 and 90 days
Workloads that were running carry on as before
The account itself is removed automatically

slots.label: As soon as the cancellation is confirmed
When the account's billing month comes to an end
Once the required waiting period after cancellation has passed
At the end of the retention window

explanation.correct: Billing stops immediately once the cancellation is confirmed, so charging for usage ends at that point even though the portal can take up to ten minutes to show it. The invoice for the usage already consumed follows the usual invoice date at the end of the billing month, and for a final subscription that cycle is closed within 72 hours, or three calendar days. The manual Delete option is only offered three days after cancellation for a customer-led subscription. Data is kept temporarily at no charge and is then permanently destroyed somewhere between 30 and 90 days later.

perChoice.i1: Belongs with the first point: after the cancellation completes, billing stops immediately.
perChoice.i2: Belongs with the second point: the final invoice is issued on the usual invoice date after the period ends, and for a last subscription the cycle is closed within 72 hours, or three calendar days.
perChoice.i3: Belongs with the third point: the Delete subscription option isn't available until three days after you cancel a customer-led subscription.
perChoice.i4: Belongs with the fourth point: Microsoft waits 30 to 90 days before permanently deleting the retained data, and you're not charged while it's kept.
perChoice.i5: Fits no slot: after cancellation your services are disabled, so virtual machines are deallocated, temporary IP addresses are freed and storage becomes read-only.
perChoice.i6: Fits no slot: Azure never automatically deletes your Azure account, so nothing here removes it automatically.

body.stem: You canceled a subscription last week and want it removed completely, but the delete page still reports objects in the way. Match each action below to the check it resolves.

items.text: Select Show hidden types from Manage view on the Resources page, then delete what appears
Take the subscription out of the AssignableScopes list in each one
Allow about ten minutes to pass, then try again
Cancel the subscription a second time so the waiting period starts over
Have the owner press Delete from a different browser

slots.label: Things that stay behind even after you think you've cleared everything
Custom roles your organization authored
The moment right after you finish removing resources

explanation.correct: The delete page can still report objects after you have cleared everything you can see, because active hidden resources aren't listed by default; showing them through Manage view and Show hidden types on the subscription's Resources page lets you delete them. Custom role definitions that name this subscription in AssignableScopes have to be edited so the subscription is dropped from that list, otherwise they can throw errors. And once you've deleted resources, the deletion status may need about ten minutes to update before the subscription delete goes through.

perChoice.i1: Resolves the first check: if you've deleted all resources but the page still shows active ones, they may be hidden types that only appear after you choose Show hidden types from Manage view.
perChoice.i2: Resolves the second check: custom roles that reference the subscription in AssignableScopes should be updated to remove it, since updating them after the subscription is canceled can produce an error.
perChoice.i3: Resolves the third check: after resource deletion you might need to wait 10 minutes for the resource deletion status to update before the subscription can be deleted.
perChoice.i4: Fits no slot: repeating the cancellation doesn't restart anything, and the checks on the delete page aren't affected by it.
perChoice.i5: Fits no slot: you need the Subscription Owner role to see and use Delete, but doing it from another browser changes nothing about the outstanding checks.

body.stem: You are about to hand a pay-as-you-go subscription over to a colleague who has a different account. Match each statement below to the rule that governs the request you send.

items.text: The administrator of the account that holds the subscription
A single request
15 days from the moment it is sent
Anywhere other than a Microsoft Entra B2B or Azure AD B2C tenant
The current subscription owner, even if they hold no billing role
Two at a time, so a backup can sit behind the first
60 days, or until the new owner has read the terms

slots.label: Who may start it
How many can be in flight at once
How long it stays valid
Where the receiving account can be located

explanation.correct: Only the account administrator of the account that has the subscription can transfer ownership, so the first statement belongs with the sender rule. Only one transfer request is active at a time, so the answer to the concurrency rule is a single request. A request is valid for 15 days, after which it expires. And subscriptions can't be transferred to a Microsoft Entra B2B or Azure AD B2C tenant, so the destination is anywhere other than those directory types.

perChoice.i1: Belongs with the sender rule: only the account administrator of the account that holds the subscription can transfer ownership.
perChoice.i2: Belongs with the concurrency rule: only one transfer request is active at a time.
perChoice.i3: Belongs with the validity rule: a transfer request is valid for 15 days and expires afterwards.
perChoice.i4: Belongs with the destination rule: subscriptions can't be transferred to a Microsoft Entra B2B or Azure AD B2C tenant.
perChoice.i5: Fits no slot: being the subscription owner isn't enough on its own; the account administrator of the account that holds the subscription is the one who can send the request.
perChoice.i6: Fits no slot: only one transfer request can be active at a time, so a second one can't sit behind it.
perChoice.i7: Fits no slot: the request is valid for 15 days; reading the terms and conditions doesn't extend or reset that period.

body.stem: Your company is leaving Azure and taking all of its data to another provider, and your support request with the intended transfer start date is already logged. Match each statement below to the requirement it satisfies.

items.text: 60 days for most customers
180 days, available to customers billed to a UK address
Cancel all subscriptions associated with the account
No fixed period — it depends on how much data you move
Wait for written confirmation before anything else

slots.label: How long you have to move the data out once your start date is logged
The extended window reserved for one country's customers
What you must do once the data is out

explanation.correct: Free egress requires advance notice through a support request, and once the request is logged you have 60 days from the start data transfer date you supplied to move the data out, so the first statement fits the general window. Customers with a UK billing address that take their data from UK datacenters get 180 days instead, so the second statement fits the extended window. After the data has been moved out, you must cancel all subscriptions associated with the account, which is what the third statement covers.

perChoice.i1: Fits the general window: after the request is logged you have 60 days from the start data transfer date you indicated to egress your data out of Azure.
perChoice.i2: Fits the extended window: customers with a billing address in the UK that transfer data from UK datacenters have 180 days.
perChoice.i3: Fits the closing step: after egressing your data you cancel all subscriptions associated with your account, and that's also required before an invoice-level credit can be requested.
perChoice.i4: Fits no slot: the offer works with fixed deadlines — 60 days for everyone and 180 days for the UK case — not an amount that scales with the data volume.
perChoice.i5: Fits no slot: no written confirmation is part of the process; the credit is reviewed against the documented requirements after you follow the stated steps.

body.stem: Your team owns the Azure billing relationships listed below, and a compliance review of each one is due this month. You need to work out the current state of every line before the review, so that nothing is left pending. Match each subscription to the statement that describes where it stands today.

columns: Role held by the person doing the review
rows: Canceled 5 days ago; no resources remaining
Canceled 5 days ago; no resources remaining
Canceled 6 days ago; no resources remaining
Disabled Access to Azure Active Directory
Still active; a billing ownership transfer request was sent 16 days ago and hasn't been answered

slots.label: Deletion can be done today
Deletion can be done after a short wait
Deletion is blocked until a permission is granted
It is removed by Microsoft without further action
The request to the other account is void and must be created again

explanation.correct: sub-2210 can be deleted now, because the Delete subscription option becomes available 3 days after cancellation for customer led subscriptions, five days have passed, no resources remain, and the reviewer already holds the Subscription Owner role. The other lines differ in exactly one respect each: sub-2211 sits in the field and partner channel, where the option only appears 7 days after cancellation, so two more days of waiting are needed; sub-2212 qualifies on timing and resources, but the Delete option can only be seen and used by someone assigned the Subscription Owner role, so a billing account contributor has to be given that assignment first; sub-2213 is a disabled Access to Azure Active Directory subscription, which is deleted automatically 90 days after cancellation with no manual step; and sub-2214's billing ownership transfer request is only valid for 15 days, so after 16 days it has expired and a new request has to be sent (only one transfer request is active at a time).

perChoice.i1: Customer led, canceled 5 days ago with no resources left and a Subscription Owner on hand: the 3 day wait for customer led subscriptions has passed, so the subscription can be deleted today.
perChoice.i2: Field and partner channel subscriptions only make the Delete subscription option available 7 days after cancellation, so with only 5 days elapsed the reviewer must wait a couple more days.
perChoice.i3: The role gate applies here rather than a timing gate: the Delete option is shown only to someone assigned the Subscription Owner role, and a billing account contributor can't see or use it until that assignment is added.
perChoice.i4: A disabled Access to Azure Active Directory subscription is deleted by Microsoft automatically 90 days after cancellation; at 60 days nothing needs to be done manually.
perChoice.i5: A billing ownership transfer request is valid for 15 days and then expires, so the recipient can no longer accept this one and the sender has to submit a new request.

body.stem: You sent a billing ownership transfer request for the subscription shown below to an administrator of another account. Today, the subscription's Transfer billing ownership page no longer lists a request that is waiting for a reply. You need to explain the situation to your colleague. Which statement is accurate?

rows: Requests shown as active on the page

body.statement: The explanation you should give your colleague is {{status}}.

options.text: The request was valid for 7 days, and it has ended.
The request was valid for 15 days, and it has ended.
The request was valid for 30 days, and it has ended.
The request stays valid for 15 days until the recipient accepts it.

explanation.correct: A transfer request is valid for 15 days; after that period it expires, so a request sent on October 1 is no longer active on October 21. Only one transfer request can be active at a time, so a new request would have to be sent.

perChoice.status:a: The window for a billing ownership transfer request is 15 days, not 7 days, so the request could not still be pending after 20 days.
perChoice.status:c: The window for a billing ownership transfer request is 15 days, not 30 days, so it expired long before October 21.
perChoice.status:d: A transfer request expires on its own after 15 days; it isn't held open indefinitely waiting for the recipient.

body.stem: You canceled a pay-as-you-go subscription yesterday, and your compliance team has assumed that everything it held was erased the moment the cancellation completed. You need to correct that assumption. Which statement is accurate?
body.statement: The statement you should give your compliance team is {{outcome}}.

options.text: Your data is kept for a while and then permanently deleted 30 to 90 days after the cancellation, and you aren't charged for the kept data.
Your data is kept for a while and then permanently deleted 7 days after the cancellation, and you aren't charged for the kept data.
Your data is erased as soon as the cancellation completes, and you receive a refund for the unused days of the billing period.
Your data is kept for a while and then permanently deleted 30 to 90 days after the cancellation, and you're charged for the kept data.

explanation.correct: Azure doesn't delete your data immediately when you cancel. Data is preserved temporarily, and Microsoft waits 30 to 90 days before permanently deleting it, without charging for the retained data. The read-only access shown in the table is the effect of cancellation, where services are disabled, and it isn't evidence that the data is gone.

perChoice.outcome:b: Permanent deletion of the data happens 30 to 90 days after the cancellation, not 7 days.
perChoice.outcome:c: Azure doesn't erase your data as soon as you cancel; it keeps it temporarily in case you reactivate the subscription, and canceling doesn't give back the unused days of the billing period.
perChoice.outcome:d: You aren't charged for data that is kept temporarily after a cancellation, so this option states the wrong billing behavior.

body.stem: Your organization's billing account is the one shown below. A colleague signed in expecting to attach an Azure subscription to it and found that the option wasn't available. You need to tell your colleague what to do instead. Which statement is accurate?

rows: Site the colleague signed in at
Option to attach an Azure subscription there

body.statement: The explanation you should give your colleague is {{path}}.

options.text: New Azure subscriptions for that billing account are no longer created at the website; you create them from the Subscriptions page in the Azure portal.
New Azure subscriptions for that billing account are only created when the account also has an Azure plan; you create them from Cost Management + Billing.
New Azure subscriptions for that billing account are only created by the account administrator; you create them from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
New Azure subscriptions for that billing account are only created during an open billing period; you create them from the Subscriptions page in the Azure portal.

explanation.correct: A Microsoft Online Services Program (MOSP) billing account is no longer able to add Azure subscriptions at https://signup.azure.com/. Subscriptions for this account type are created from the Subscriptions page in the Azure portal instead, where the billing account, billing profile, and invoice section are selected.

perChoice.path:b: An Azure plan on the account isn't the deciding factor; that site doesn't offer this for a MOSP billing account at all.
perChoice.path:c: Only the account administrator isn't the deciding factor; the Microsoft 365 admin center isn't where these subscriptions are created.
perChoice.path:d: The billing period isn't the deciding factor; that site doesn't offer this for a MOSP billing account at all.

body.stem: You are creating an Azure subscription for your team from the portal. On the Advanced tab you must list one or more owners, and one of the people you want to give ownership to is a colleague who works for a partner firm and accepted an invitation to collaborate with your organization. Which statement explains what you can enter in that field?

options.text: Only users or service principals that belong to the chosen directory can be put there.
Users, service principals, and guest directory users can all be put there.
Any invited external collaborator can be put there, but only after the invitation is accepted.
Users or service principals from any directory can be put there, including guests.

explanation.correct: In the Create a subscription flow, the owners field accepts only users or service principals from the subscription directory that you picked on the Advanced tab. Guest directory users can't be added as subscription owners, so an external collaborator from a partner firm can't be entered there.

perChoice.owners:b: Guest directory users can't be selected as subscription owners, so they can't be added to this field.
perChoice.owners:c: Accepting an invitation doesn't make a guest directory user selectable in the owners field; that list only offers users or service principals from the subscription directory.
perChoice.owners:d: The users and service principals available are the ones from the subscription directory you selected, not identities from any directory, and guests aren't available at all.

body.stem: Your pay-as-you-go subscription has an Azure support plan that no other subscription uses. When you start the cancellation in the portal, the plan appears in the flow with a Turn off auto-renew option. Your finance lead expects a partial refund for the days of the plan you won't use. Which statement is accurate?

rows: Plan option shown in the flow

body.statement: The statement you should give your finance lead is {{charge}}.

options.text: You're billed for the rest of the month, because canceling a support plan doesn't result in a prorated refund.
You receive a prorated refund, because canceling a support plan results in a prorated refund.
You're not billed again after today, because canceling a support plan ends the charges for it immediately.
You receive a full refund for the plan, because canceling a subscription refunds the support plan it includes.

explanation.correct: Canceling an Azure support plan bills you for the rest of the month, and canceling doesn't produce a prorated refund. Turning off auto-renew only stops the plan from renewing; it doesn't return the remaining amount for the current period.

perChoice.charge:b: A support plan cancellation doesn't result in a prorated refund; you're still billed for the remainder of the current period.
perChoice.charge:c: The charges for the plan continue to the end of the current period, so you are billed again after today even though auto-renew is turned off.
perChoice.charge:d: Canceling the subscription doesn't refund the associated support plan; the plan is simply canceled and billed for the rest of the month.

body.stem: Your organization buys Azure through an Enterprise Agreement. Last week an administrator canceled subscription sub-5118 by mistake, and the production workloads behind it need to be available again. Which statement describes how to bring the subscription back?
body.statement: To get subscription sub-5118 running again, you should {{action}}.

options.text: Contact Microsoft support within 90 days of the cancellation
Contact Microsoft support within 30 days of the cancellation
Contact Microsoft support within 60 days of the cancellation
Reactivate the subscription yourself in the Azure portal

explanation.correct: Self-service reactivation in the Azure portal is available only for a subscription that was canceled with pay-as-you-go rates. Subscription sub-5118 is covered by an Enterprise Agreement, so it is not a pay-as-you-go subscription; the documented route for such a subscription is to contact Microsoft support, and that request must be made within 90 days of the cancellation for the subscription to be reactivated.

perChoice.action:b: 30 days is not the deadline that applies here. For a canceled subscription that is not pay-as-you-go, the reactivation request to support must be raised within 90 days of the cancellation, not 30.
perChoice.action:c: 60 days is likewise not a documented reactivation deadline; the support request for a non-pay-as-you-go subscription is valid only within 90 days of the cancellation.
perChoice.action:d: Reactivating a canceled subscription yourself in the portal applies to subscriptions canceled with pay-as-you-go rates. An Enterprise Agreement subscription such as this one has to be reactivated through Microsoft support instead.
